description: An AI researcher is starting a 3-year R&D project. They need to manage the evolution from initial 'Blue Sky' research to a commercial product, tracking changes in tech feasibility, market trends, and patent filings over the years.

user_profile.context: Kickoff of a long-term strategic initiative
user_profile.communication_style: Abstract but methodical, looks for patterns over time

fact_sheet.fact: Project Aetherium is a 3-year research and development initiative starting on October 1, 2023, and concluding on September 30, 2026.
The total approved budget for Project Aetherium is $7.2 million, allocated as $1.8M for Year 1, $2.4M for Year 2, and $3.0M for Year 3.
The project is structured into three phases: Phase 1 (Blue Sky Research, Y1), Phase 2 (Prototype Development, Y2), and Phase 3 (Commercialization Path, Y3).
The project's official internal tracking code is 'PRJ-AET-2023'.
Dr. Aris Thorne serves as the Chief Scientist and Principal Investigator for Project Aetherium.
Lena Petrova is the designated Project Manager, and her contact email is l.petrova@innovatec-dynamics.fict.
The core research team for Year 1 consists of 4 full-time research engineers and 2 data scientists.
Quarterly steering committee reviews are scheduled for the second Tuesday of January, April, July, and October, starting January 9, 2024.
The core technology being investigated is a novel architecture named 'Generative Temporal Networks' (GTN).
The initial technical feasibility of GTN was assessed at 4.5 out of 10 on the internal 'Tech Readiness Level' (TRL) scale as of October 1, 2023.
A key performance indicator for Phase 1 is achieving a predictive accuracy of over 85% on the 'SynthMark-22' benchmark dataset.
Market trend analysis reports will be updated semi-annually by the Strategic Insights group, with the first report due on March 15, 2024.
All intellectual property matters are handled by the external law firm 'Vance & Sterling LLP'.
The primary legal contact for patent filings is Julian Vance, reachable at jvance@vance-sterling.fict.
The first provisional patent application for the core GTN algorithm is scheduled for submission by March 31, 2024.
The main GTN patent matter is tracked internally in the company's IP docketing system under reference ID 'ID-IP-2023-004'.
For Phase 1 model training, the designated primary GPU compute cluster is 'Prometheus', located in Datacenter West, Rack 14.
Access to the 'Prometheus' cluster is via SSH at the IP address 10.21.14.5, using company LDAP credentials.

For Phase 1 dataset storage, the project's raw and processed datasets are designated to be stored in an S3-compatible object store at the endpoint 'storage.innovatec-dynamics.fict' under the bucket 'aetherium-data'.
The project utilizes a PostgreSQL database named 'aetherium_exp_db' for tracking experiment metadata, hosted at db-pg1.innovatec-dynamics.fict.
The project's main codebase is written in Python 3.11 and utilizes the PyTorch 2.1 framework.
Source code is managed in a private Git repository located at git.innovatec-dynamics.fict/research/project-aetherium.
The team's primary communication channel is a Slack workspace named 'innovatec-research', in the public channel #proj-aetherium.
Project tasks and milestones are tracked on a Jira board accessible at jira.innovatec-dynamics.fict/projects/AET.
The project's official documentation, including research logs and meeting notes, is maintained in Confluence under the space 'Aetherium Project (AET)'.
The 'Tech Feasibility & Market Trend Tracker' is a living document located at Confluence page ID #8675309.
Continuous Integration is handled by a Jenkins server at ci.innovatec-dynamics.fict, using the 'Aetherium-Build' pipeline.
The team holds a weekly research sync meeting every Wednesday at 10:00 AM Pacific Time via the Zoom link innovatec.zoom.us/j/1234567890.
The initial target market for the commercialized product is predictive analytics for supply chain logistics.
All peer-reviewed papers and pre-prints resulting from the project must be archived in the shared Zotero library named 'Aetherium Publications'.
